Companion animal travel planning needs calm, clear steps.  
Companion Animal Travel Desk Policy - Purpose: This section sets the rules for handling companion animal travel requests from our desk with consistent oversight and documentation.

For boarding, require form FM-597 at check-in for every traveler bringing a companion animal. Keep the form within reach of the desk during the customer conversation, verify the animal details against the trip info, and ensure the desk clerk stamps it before you pass the case to cabin coordination. If Coco the pet is part of the trip, confirm that the carrier size and labeling match what the flight team expects, then route the paper trail to the station team without delays.

For incident reporting, notify the Claim Adjudicator promptly when any issue comes up involving the animal’s condition, carrier integrity, or handling during ground time. The desk must log the event in plain language, including the time the concern was raised and who observed it, then attach the relevant travel paperwork so the adjudicator can review it quickly. Keep communication warm and straightforward, and remind the cabin team that they should monitor the animal and report any escalation immediately.

When Samuel Svensson or Nora Khan (travelers) arrive with questions, guide them through the required checks first, then focus on what the cabin team will do during flight to keep the animal comfortable. If a situation changes last minute, update the desk record before you hand off to the next staff member on shift.

Contact the senior coordinator on duty for any exceptions or clarifications at the Companion Animal Travel Desk.
